summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph — run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum production code to make the test PASS
— no over-engineering
— simplest possible implementation"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up code while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— apply OOP principles
— run tests after every change"] T4{"More requirements to implement?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next behavior"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All behaviors implemented with tests]) end subgraph RULES["TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER write production code without a failing test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more production code than needed to pass the test"] R3["✅ Tests must be fast, isolated, and deterministic"] R4["✅ Aim for 100% unit test coverage on new and modified code"] R5["✅ When behavior involves a loop/collection, add a case with 2+ items, not only a single-item happy path — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still wrong"] R6["✅ Run the full test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## Where to write TDD tests Write failing unit / widget tests in the project's standard unit-test tree **only**: - Flutter / Dart projects → `test/` - Node projects → `__tests__/` or `test/` according to the repo convention - Python projects → `tests/` or project-specific unit-test directory ❌ **Never** place development TDD tests under `testing/`. `testing/` is owned by test-automation agents (regression probes, workflow observation tests, accessibility gates, etc.). So workflowFailureReporter.action has zero coverage → CRAP = CC²+CC = 128.1 means CC=11 (11²+11=132... no). 128.1: solve c²+c=128.1? c=11 → 132; c=10 → 110. Not integer — CRAP formula includes coverage: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov/100)³ + CC. With 0% coverage, 128.1 → c(c+1)=128.1, c≈10.8. Hmm, maybe fractional because... Actually with cov>0: c²(1-f)³+c = 128.1. If c=11: 121·(1-f)³+11=128.1 → (1-f)³=0.968 → f≈1%. OK whatever.

For detectFailedChecks 86.9: c²(1-f)³+c=86.9. c=9: 81(1-f)³+9=86.9 → (1-f)³=0.962 → f≈1.3%. So both have tiny coverage, CC≈11 and CC≈9.

Goal: bring each under CRAP 30. Options: reduce CC by extracting helpers AND/OR raise coverage. "Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it."

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

blocks.text:
While the baseline measurement runs, let me design the refactor and write the tests (TDD: write characterization tests for uncovered branches first).

**Plan for `githubHelpers.detectFailedChecks`:**

Extract pure helpers (all ≤ CC 8, each tiny):

1. `normalizeCheckRunsResult(rawResult)` — parse string, extract array. (CC small)
2. `isFailedCheck(c)` — conclusion failure/timed_out.
3. `appendLogSection(md, fullLogContent, check, logs, label)` → returns {md, fullLogContent} or mutates an accumulator object. Make it pure: takes (check, logs, label) returns {mdSection, fullLogSection} or null.
4. `normalizeLogPayload(raw)` — parse JSON {result} wrapper. (pure)
5. `extractJenkinsTarget(detailsUrl, jenkinsBasePath)` → {jobPath, buildNumber} or null. (pure, CC ~4)
6. `buildCiFailuresMarkdown(failedChecks, headSha, logSections)` — pure builder.
7. `buildResolutionSection()` — constant.

Then detectFailedChecks keeps orchestration: dual-mode arg parse, headSha check, fetch (scm vs direct), null checks, loop calling helpers, try/catch.

But note the ratchet: "new functions must be ≤ 8" and "target functions must go DOWN, no function may go UP". detectFailedChecks CC is ~11; after extraction, remaining branches: try/catch + 2 arg branches + headSha + scm-null + string-parse (moved out) + array extraction (moved out) + no checks + no failures + loop + jobIdMatch + jenkins condition + jenkins inner... Actually if I extract the Jenkins block into `fetchJenkinsLogs(check, jenkinsBasePath)` (CC ~3: guard conditions + loop... the digit-detection loop is a for with 2 branches) and the github-job-logs block into `fetchJobLogs(check, scm, owner, repo)` (CC ~3), the main function drops a lot.

Even better for CRAP: raising coverage counts too. The existing tests cover some Jenkins paths. I'll add characterization tests for: scm-mode invocation, job logs via /jobs/(\d+) match (github + scm), JSON-wrapped logs, no-failures, no checks, null rawResult, string rawResult, unparseable string, headSha missing, overall catch.

**Plan for `workflowFailureReporter.action`:**

Extract helpers:

1. `parseWorkflowRuns(runsRaw)` → {runs: [...]} or {error: '...'} — handles string parse + workflow_runs extraction. (CC ~3)
2. `extractTicketKey(runName)` → key or null. (CC ~1)
3. `buildBugSummary(run, workflowId)` — pure. (CC ~2)
4. `buildBugDescription(run, runWorkflow, ticketKey)` — pure. (CC ~2)
5. `extractCreatedKey(result)` → key or null — handles string JSON, bare key, /browse/ URL, object .key. (CC ~4)
6. `processRun(run, ctx)` — the per-run pipeline (label search, ticket key, open bug, create, label, link). CC still highish but separate; and action's CC drops. Actually to be safe under the ratchet for the NEW function (≤8), processRun has: existing.length check, ticketMatch, ticketKey, openBug check, newKey check, ticketKey link/label, try/catch... that's ~8-9. Hmm. Could split further: `findExistingBug(runId)`, `shouldSkipForOpenTicket(ticketKey)`. But those need tracker access. Alternatively pass ctx with tracker.

Actually, CRAP ≤ 30 for target functions only required; NEW functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP, not CC. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³+CC. With full coverage CRAP = CC. So new function with CC 8 fully covered = 8 ✓. With CC 9 fully covered = 9 ✗. So keep new functions at CC ≤ 8, and cover them.

processRun: branches: existing>0 (skip), ticketKey null?, openBug>0 (skip), newKey null, addLabel try/catch (catch adds branch? try/catch counts as a branch in most CC tools — crap4js based on escomplex? Unknown. Assume try/catch counts). Let me count conservatively and split:

- `findLabeledBug(tracker, jiraProject, label)` → array or [] (with try/catch inside, CC ~2)
- `detectTicketKey(runName)` → CC 1
- `hasOpenTicketBug(tracker, jiraProject, ticketKey)` → CC ~2
- `createBugForRun(tracker, jiraProject, run, workflowId, ticketKey, label)` → does create + extract key + labels + link, returns key or null; CC ~6-7 (try/catch around create, newKey check, addLabel try/catch, ticketKey link try/catch, addLabel try/catch). Hmm that's 5+ decisions. Maybe further split `applyBugLinks(tracker, newKey, ticketKey, label)` CC ~3.

Then `processRun(run, ctx)` CC: existing check, ticketKey check, openBug check, key null check → ~4-5. And action: param check, runsRaw null, parse error, empty, loop → ~5.

Alternatively simpler: since raising coverage counts as much as splitting, and the ratchet only requires target CRAP < 30 (from 128.1 / 86.9), I could just write thorough characterization tests achieving high coverage on both functions without any refactor. CRAP with c=11 and cov f: 121(1-f)³+11. For CRAP=30: (1-f)³=19/121=0.157 → f≈46%. So ~50% coverage of detectFailedChecks/action brings them under 30. But the "no function may go UP" gate — no changes needed then. And new functions none.

However the ticket title says "Extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*)" — the ticket's approach is extraction + tests. The AC: "CRAP of both target functions goes down (below the 30 threshold)". Both approaches satisfy. But wait — there's a subtlety with the ratchet: it compares per-function CRAP by name against the released baseline. If I don't refactor, function names stay the same; coverage increases; CRAP goes down. That passes.

But is pure test-only change in the spirit? The ticket explicitly prescribes "Extract pure helpers". Also CRAP thresholds: the quality workflow blocks merge only when functions exceed threshold AND are worse than baseline... Actually the ratchet fails when any function is worse than baseline? Let me recall typical crap4js ratchet semantics: it fails if any function's CRAP exceeds threshold (30) and is not in baseline with same/higher CRAP; improved functions reported. Target: both under 30.

Given "both": extraction reduces CC structurally (more robust against future coverage gaps) and matches the ticket. I'll do extraction + tests, keeping behavior byte-identical in outputs. But every extraction creates NEW functions that must be ≤ 8 CRAP — they're tiny and will be covered by tests.

One concern: exporting helpers for tests. githubHelpers exports many functions; I'll add new exports. workflowFailureReporter exports only action; I'll add helper exports.

Also: "Do not weaken the ratchet, thresholds, or coverage collection" — fine.

Also the pack release test gate: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` must be green; pack_release_guard checks released pack integrity — I'm not touching packs. instructionRefs test may verify referenced files exist — I'm not changing references.

Note: there might be a test that asserts workflowFailureReporter exports only {action}? Let me check test files referencing it — grep showed test files containing "workflowFailureReporter": test_wave2d4Tracker.js, test_preparePRForReview.js, test_machineNotice.js, test_preCliReworkSetup.js — probably just string mentions in fixtures. Let me check quickly.

Now, TDD order: write characterization tests FIRST for the current behavior (they should pass on current code since no behavior change... hmm, TDD RED requires failing first). The honest TDD approach here: tests for the NEW helper functions fail first (helpers don't exist yet), then implement. Plus characterization tests for action/detectFailedChecks branches — these pass immediately on current code (not RED). That's acceptable: the RED step is for new helpers. I'll write helper tests first (RED: loadModule fails — undefined export), then refactor.

Let me check the grep hits for workflowFailureReporter in test files to be safe.

So workflowFailureReporter.action has zero coverage → CRAP = CC²+CC = 128.1 means CC=11 (11²+11=132... no). 128.1: solve c²+c=128.1? c=11 → 132; c=10 → 110. Not integer — CRAP formula includes coverage: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov/100)³ + CC. With 0% coverage, 128.1 → c(c+1)=128.1, c≈10.8. Hmm, maybe fractional because... Actually with cov>0: c²(1-f)³+c = 128.1. For detectFailedChecks 86.9: c²(1-f)³+c=86.9. c=9: 81(1-f)³+9=86.9 → (1-f)³=0.962 → f≈1.3%. So both have tiny coverage, CC≈11 and CC≈9.

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

While the baseline measurement runs, let me design the refactor and write the tests (TDD: write characterization tests for uncovered branches first).

**Plan for `githubHelpers.detectFailedChecks`:**

Extract pure helpers (all ≤ CC 8, each tiny):

1. `normalizeCheckRunsResult(rawResult)` — parse string, extract array. (CC small)
2. `isFailedCheck(c)` — conclusion failure/timed_out.
3. `appendLogSection(md, fullLogContent, check, logs, label)` → returns {md, fullLogContent} or mutates an accumulator object. Make it pure: takes (check, logs, label) returns {mdSection, fullLogSection} or null.
4. `normalizeLogPayload(raw)` — parse JSON {result} wrapper. (pure)
5. `extractJenkinsTarget(detailsUrl, jenkinsBasePath)` → {jobPath, buildNumber} or null. (pure, CC ~4)
6. `buildCiFailuresMarkdown(failedChecks, headSha, logSections)` — pure builder.
7. `buildResolutionSection()` — constant.

Then detectFailedChecks keeps orchestration: dual-mode arg parse, headSha check, fetch (scm vs direct), null checks, loop calling helpers, try/catch.

But note the ratchet: "new functions must be ≤ 8" and "target functions must go DOWN, no function may go UP". detectFailedChecks CC is ~11; after extraction, remaining branches: try/catch + 2 arg branches + headSha + scm-null + string-parse (moved out) + array extraction (moved out) + no checks + no failures + loop + jobIdMatch + jenkins condition + jenkins inner... Actually if I extract the Jenkins block into `fetchJenkinsLogs(check, jenkinsBasePath)` (CC ~3: guard conditions + loop... the digit-detection loop is a for with 2 branches) and the github-job-logs block into `fetchJobLogs(check, scm, owner, repo)` (CC ~3), the main function drops a lot.

Even better for CRAP: raising coverage counts too. The existing tests cover some Jenkins paths. I'll add characterization tests for: scm-mode invocation, job logs via /jobs/(\d+) match (github + scm), JSON-wrapped logs, no-failures, no checks, null rawResult, string rawResult, unparseable string, headSha missing, overall catch.

**Plan for `workflowFailureReporter.action`:**

Extract helpers:

1. `parseWorkflowRuns(runsRaw)` → {runs: [...]} or {error: '...'} — handles string parse + workflow_runs extraction. (CC ~3)
2. `extractTicketKey(runName)` → key or null. (CC ~1)
3. `buildBugSummary(run, workflowId)` — pure. (CC ~2)
4. `buildBugDescription(run, runWorkflow, ticketKey)` — pure. (CC ~2)
5. `extractCreatedKey(result)` → key or null — handles string JSON, bare key, /browse/ URL, object .key. (CC ~4)
6. `processRun(run, ctx)` — the per-run pipeline (label search, ticket key, open bug, create, label, link). CC still highish but separate; and action's CC drops. Actually to be safe under the ratchet for the NEW function (≤8), processRun has: existing.length check, ticketMatch, ticketKey, openBug check, newKey check, ticketKey link/label, try/catch... that's ~8-9. Hmm. Could split further: `findExistingBug(runId)`, `shouldSkipForOpenTicket(ticketKey)`. But those need tracker access. Alternatively pass ctx with tracker.

Actually, CRAP ≤ 30 for target functions only required; NEW functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP, not CC. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³+CC. With full coverage CRAP = CC. So new function with CC 8 fully covered = 8 ✓. With CC 9 fully covered = 9 ✗. So keep new functions at CC ≤ 8, and cover them.

processRun: branches: existing>0 (skip), ticketKey null?, openBug>0 (skip), newKey null, addLabel try/catch (catch adds branch? try/catch counts as a branch in most CC tools — crap4js based on escomplex? Unknown. Assume try/catch counts). Let me count conservatively and split:

- `findLabeledBug(tracker, jiraProject, label)` → array or [] (with try/catch inside, CC ~2)
- `detectTicketKey(runName)` → CC 1
- `hasOpenTicketBug(tracker, jiraProject, ticketKey)` → CC ~2
- `createBugForRun(tracker, jiraProject, run, workflowId, ticketKey, label)` → does create + extract key + labels + link, returns key or null; CC ~6-7 (try/catch around create, newKey check, addLabel try/catch, ticketKey link try/catch, addLabel try/catch). Hmm that's 5+ decisions. Maybe further split `applyBugLinks(tracker, newKey, ticketKey, label)` CC ~3.

Then `processRun(run, ctx)` CC: existing check, ticketKey check, openBug check, key null check → ~4-5. And action: param check, runsRaw null, parse error, empty, loop → ~5.

Alternatively simpler: since raising coverage counts as much as splitting, and the ratchet only requires target CRAP < 30 (from 128.1 / 86.9), I could just write thorough characterization tests achieving high coverage on both functions without any refactor. CRAP with c=11 and cov f: 121(1-f)³+11. For CRAP=30: (1-f)³=19/121=0.157 → f≈46%. So ~50% coverage of detectFailedChecks/action brings them under 30. But the "no function may go UP" gate — no changes needed then. And new functions none.

However the ticket title says "Extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*)" — the ticket's approach is extraction + tests. The AC: "CRAP of both target functions goes down (below the 30 threshold)". Both approaches satisfy. But wait — there's a subtlety with the ratchet: it compares per-function CRAP by name against the released baseline. If I don't refactor, function names stay the same; coverage increases; CRAP goes down. That passes.

But is pure test-only change in the spirit? The ticket explicitly prescribes "Extract pure helpers". Also CRAP thresholds: the quality workflow blocks merge only when functions exceed threshold AND are worse than baseline... Actually the ratchet fails when any function is worse than baseline? Let me recall typical crap4js ratchet semantics: it fails if any function's CRAP exceeds threshold (30) and is not in baseline with same/higher CRAP; improved functions reported. Target: both under 30.

Given "both": extraction reduces CC structurally (more robust against future coverage gaps) and matches the ticket. I'll do extraction + tests, keeping behavior byte-identical in outputs. But every extraction creates NEW functions that must be ≤ 8 CRAP — they're tiny and will be covered by tests.

One concern: exporting helpers for tests. githubHelpers exports many functions; I'll add new exports. workflowFailureReporter exports only action; I'll add helper exports.

Also: "Do not weaken the ratchet, thresholds, or coverage collection" — fine.

Also the pack release test gate: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` must be green; pack_release_guard checks released pack integrity — I'm not touching packs. instructionRefs test may verify referenced files exist — I'm not changing references.

Note: there might be a test that asserts workflowFailureReporter exports only {action}? Let me check test files referencing it — grep showed test files containing "workflowFailureReporter": test_wave2d4Tracker.js, test_preparePRForReview.js, test_machineNotice.js, test_preCliReworkSetup.js — probably just string mentions in fixtures. The honest TDD approach here: tests for the NEW helper functions fail first (helpers don't exist yet), then implement. --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph   crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

blocks.text:
While the baseline measurement runs, let me design the refactor and write the tests (TDD: write characterization tests for uncovered branches first).

**Plan for `githubHelpers.detectFailedChecks`:**

Extract pure helpers (all ≤ CC 8, each tiny):

1. `normalizeCheckRunsResult(rawResult)` — parse string, extract array. (CC small)
2. `isFailedCheck(c)` — conclusion failure/timed_out.
3. `appendLogSection(md, fullLogContent, check, logs, label)` → returns {md, fullLogContent} or mutates an accumulator object. Make it pure: takes (check, logs, label) returns {mdSection, fullLogSection} or null.
4. `normalizeLogPayload(raw)` — parse JSON {result} wrapper. (pure)
5. `extractJenkinsTarget(detailsUrl, jenkinsBasePath)` → {jobPath, buildNumber} or null. (pure, CC ~4)
6. `buildCiFailuresMarkdown(failedChecks, headSha, logSections)` — pure builder.
7. `buildResolutionSection()` — constant.

Then detectFailedChecks keeps orchestration: dual-mode arg parse, headSha check, fetch (scm vs direct), null checks, loop calling helpers, try/catch.

But note the ratchet: "new functions must be ≤ 8" and "target functions must go DOWN, no function may go UP". detectFailedChecks CC is ~11; after extraction, remaining branches: try/catch + 2 arg branches + headSha + scm-null + string-parse (moved out) + array extraction (moved out) + no checks + no failures + loop + jobIdMatch + jenkins condition + jenkins inner... Actually if I extract the Jenkins block into `fetchJenkinsLogs(check, jenkinsBasePath)` (CC ~3: guard conditions + loop... the digit-detection loop is a for with 2 branches) and the github-job-logs block into `fetchJobLogs(check, scm, owner, repo)` (CC ~3), the main function drops a lot.

Even better for CRAP: raising coverage counts too. The existing tests cover some Jenkins paths. I'll add characterization tests for: scm-mode invocation, job logs via /jobs/(\d+) match (github + scm), JSON-wrapped logs, no-failures, no checks, null rawResult, string rawResult, unparseable string, headSha missing, overall catch.

**Plan for `workflowFailureReporter.action`:**

Extract helpers:

1. `parseWorkflowRuns(runsRaw)` → {runs: [...]} or {error: '...'} — handles string parse + workflow_runs extraction. (CC ~3)
2. `extractTicketKey(runName)` → key or null. (CC ~1)
3. `buildBugSummary(run, workflowId)` — pure. (CC ~2)
4. `buildBugDescription(run, runWorkflow, ticketKey)` — pure. (CC ~2)
5. `extractCreatedKey(result)` → key or null — handles string JSON, bare key, /browse/ URL, object .key. (CC ~4)
6. `processRun(run, ctx)` — the per-run pipeline (label search, ticket key, open bug, create, label, link). CC still highish but separate; and action's CC drops. Actually to be safe under the ratchet for the NEW function (≤8), processRun has: existing.length check, ticketMatch, ticketKey, openBug check, newKey check, ticketKey link/label, try/catch... that's ~8-9. Hmm. Could split further: `findExistingBug(runId)`, `shouldSkipForOpenTicket(ticketKey)`. But those need tracker access. Alternatively pass ctx with tracker.

Actually, CRAP ≤ 30 for target functions only required; NEW functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP, not CC. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³+CC. With full coverage CRAP = CC. So new function with CC 8 fully covered = 8 ✓. With CC 9 fully covered = 9 ✗. So keep new functions at CC ≤ 8, and cover them.

processRun: branches: existing>0 (skip), ticketKey null?, openBug>0 (skip), newKey null, addLabel try/catch (catch adds branch? try/catch counts as a branch in most CC tools — crap4js based on escomplex? Unknown. Assume try/catch counts). Let me count conservatively and split:

- `findLabeledBug(tracker, jiraProject, label)` → array or [] (with try/catch inside, CC ~2)
- `detectTicketKey(runName)` → CC 1

Not integer — CRAP formula includes coverage: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov/100)³ + CC. With 0% coverage, 128.1 → c(c+1)=128.1, c≈10.8. Hmm, maybe fractional because... Actually with cov>0: c²(1-f)³+c = 128.1.   crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

**Plan for `githubHelpers.detectFailedChecks`:**

Extract pure helpers (all ≤ CC 8, each tiny):

1. `normalizeCheckRunsResult(rawResult)` — parse string, extract array. (CC small)
2. `isFailedCheck(c)` — conclusion failure/timed_out.
3. `appendLogSection(md, fullLogContent, check, logs, label)` → returns {md, fullLogContent} or mutates an accumulator object. Make it pure: takes (check, logs, label) returns {mdSection, fullLogSection} or null.
4. `normalizeLogPayload(raw)` — parse JSON {result} wrapper. (pure)
5. `extractJenkinsTarget(detailsUrl, jenkinsBasePath)` → {jobPath, buildNumber} or null. (pure, CC ~4)
6. `buildCiFailuresMarkdown(failedChecks, headSha, logSections)` — pure builder.
7. `buildResolutionSection()` — constant.

Then detectFailedChecks keeps orchestration: dual-mode arg parse, headSha check, fetch (scm vs direct), null checks, loop calling helpers, try/catch.

But note the ratchet: "new functions must be ≤ 8" and "target functions must go DOWN, no function may go UP". detectFailedChecks CC is ~11; after extraction, remaining branches: try/catch + 2 arg branches + headSha + scm-null + string-parse (moved out) + array extraction (moved out) + no checks + no failures + loop + jobIdMatch + jenkins condition + jenkins inner... Actually if I extract the Jenkins block into `fetchJenkinsLogs(check, jenkinsBasePath)` (CC ~3: guard conditions + loop... the digit-detection loop is a for with 2 branches) and the github-job-logs block into `fetchJobLogs(check, scm, owner, repo)` (CC ~3), the main function drops a lot.

Even better for CRAP: raising coverage counts too. The existing tests cover some Jenkins paths. I'll add characterization tests for: scm-mode invocation, job logs via /jobs/(\d+) match (github + scm), JSON-wrapped logs, no-failures, no checks, null rawResult, string rawResult, unparseable string, headSha missing, overall catch.

**Plan for `workflowFailureReporter.action`:**

Extract helpers:

1. `parseWorkflowRuns(runsRaw)` → {runs: [...]} or {error: '...'} — handles string parse + workflow_runs extraction. (CC ~3)
2. `extractTicketKey(runName)` → key or null. (CC ~1)
3. `buildBugSummary(run, workflowId)` — pure. (CC ~2)
4. `buildBugDescription(run, runWorkflow, ticketKey)` — pure. (CC ~2)
5. `extractCreatedKey(result)` → key or null — handles string JSON, bare key, /browse/ URL, object .key. (CC ~4)
6. `processRun(run, ctx)` — the per-run pipeline (label search, ticket key, open bug, create, label, link). CC still highish but separate; and action's CC drops. Actually to be safe under the ratchet for the NEW function (≤8), processRun has: existing.length check, ticketMatch, ticketKey, openBug check, newKey check, ticketKey link/label, try/catch... that's ~8-9. Hmm. Could split further: `findExistingBug(runId)`, `shouldSkipForOpenTicket(ticketKey)`. But those need tracker access. Alternatively pass ctx with tracker.

Actually, CRAP ≤ 30 for target functions only required; NEW functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP, not CC. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³+CC. With full coverage CRAP = CC. So new function with CC 8 fully covered = 8 ✓. With CC 9 fully covered = 9 ✗. So keep new functions at CC ≤ 8, and cover them.

processRun: branches: existing>0 (skip), ticketKey null?, openBug>0 (skip), newKey null, addLabel try/catch (catch adds branch? try/catch counts as a branch in most CC tools — crap4js based on escomplex? Unknown. Assume try/catch counts). Let me count conservatively and split:

- `findLabeledBug(tracker, jiraProject, label)` → array or [] (with try/catch inside, CC ~2)
- `detectTicketKey(runName)` → CC 1
- `hasOpenTicketBug(tracker, jiraProject, ticketKey)` → CC ~2
- `createBugForRun(tracker, jiraProject, run, workflowId, ticketKey, label)` → does create + extract key + labels + link, returns key or null; CC ~6-7 (try/catch around create, newKey check, addLabel try/catch, ticketKey link try/catch, addLabel try/catch). Hmm that's 5+ decisions. Maybe further split `applyBugLinks(tracker, newKey, ticketKey, label)` CC ~3.

Then `processRun(run, ctx)` CC: existing check, ticketKey check, openBug check, key null check → ~4-5. And action: param check, runsRaw null, parse error, empty, loop → ~5.

Alternatively simpler: since raising coverage counts as much as splitting, and the ratchet only requires target CRAP < 30 (from 128.1 / 86.9), I could just write thorough characterization tests achieving high coverage on both functions without any refactor. CRAP with c=11 and cov f: 121(1-f)³+11. For CRAP=30: (1-f)³=19/121=0.157 → f≈46%. So ~50% coverage of detectFailedChecks/action brings them under 30. Not integer — CRAP formula includes coverage: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov/100)³ + CC. With 0% coverage, 128.1 → c(c+1)=128.1, c≈10.8. Hmm, maybe fractional because... Actually with cov>0: c²(1-f)³+c = 128.1.   crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

blocks.text:
While the baseline measurement runs, let me design the refactor and write the tests (TDD: write characterization tests for uncovered branches first).

**Plan for `githubHelpers.detectFailedChecks`:**

Extract pure helpers (all ≤ CC 8, each tiny):

1. `normalizeCheckRunsResult(rawResult)` — parse string, extract array. (CC small)
2. `isFailedCheck(c)` — conclusion failure/timed_out.
3. `appendLogSection(md, fullLogContent, check, logs, label)` → returns {md, fullLogContent} or mutates an accumulator object. Make it pure: takes (check, logs, label) returns {mdSection, fullLogSection} or null.
4. `normalizeLogPayload(raw)` — parse JSON {result} wrapper. (pure)
5. `extractJenkinsTarget(detailsUrl, jenkinsBasePath)` → {jobPath, buildNumber} or null. (pure, CC ~4)
6. `buildCiFailuresMarkdown(failedChecks, headSha, logSections)` — pure builder.
7. `buildResolutionSection()` — constant.

Then detectFailedChecks keeps orchestration: dual-mode arg parse, headSha check, fetch (scm vs direct), null checks, loop calling helpers, try/catch.

But note the ratchet: "new functions must be ≤ 8" and "target functions must go DOWN, no function may go UP". detectFailedChecks CC is ~11; after extraction, remaining branches: try/catch + 2 arg branches + headSha + scm-null + string-parse (moved out) + array extraction (moved out) + no checks + no failures + loop + jobIdMatch + jenkins condition + jenkins inner... Actually if I extract the Jenkins block into `fetchJenkinsLogs(check, jenkinsBasePath)` (CC ~3: guard conditions + loop... the digit-detection loop is a for with 2 branches) and the github-job-logs block into `fetchJobLogs(check, scm, owner, repo)` (CC ~3), the main function drops a lot.

Even better for CRAP: raising coverage counts too. The existing tests cover some Jenkins paths. I'll add characterization tests for: scm-mode invocation, job logs via /jobs/(\d+) match (github + scm), JSON-wrapped logs, no-failures, no checks, null rawResult, string rawResult, unparseable string, headSha missing, overall catch.

**Plan for `workflowFailureReporter.action`:**

Extract helpers:

1. `parseWorkflowRuns(runsRaw)` → {runs: [...]} or {error: '...'} — handles string parse + workflow_runs extraction. (CC ~3)
2. `extractTicketKey(runName)` → key or null. (CC ~1)
3. `buildBugSummary(run, workflowId)` — pure. (CC ~2)
4. `buildBugDescription(run, runWorkflow, ticketKey)` — pure. (CC ~2)
5. `extractCreatedKey(result)` → key or null — handles string JSON, bare key, /browse/ URL, object .key. (CC ~4)
6. `processRun(run, ctx)` — the per-run pipeline (label search, ticket key, open bug, create, label, link). CC still highish but separate; and action's CC drops. Actually to be safe under the ratchet for the NEW function (≤8), processRun has: existing.length check, ticketMatch, ticketKey, openBug check, newKey check, ticketKey link/label, try/catch... that's ~8-9. Hmm. Could split further: `findExistingBug(runId)`, `shouldSkipForOpenTicket(ticketKey)`. But those need tracker access. Alternatively pass ctx with tracker.

Actually, CRAP ≤ 30 for target functions only required; NEW functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP, not CC. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³+CC. With full coverage CRAP = CC. So new function with CC 8 fully covered = 8 ✓. With CC 9 fully covered = 9 ✗. So keep new functions at CC ≤ 8, and cover them.

processRun: branches: existing>0 (skip), ticketKey null?, openBug>0 (skip), newKey null, addLabel try/catch (catch adds branch? try/catch counts as a branch in most CC tools — crap4js based on escomplex? Unknown. Assume try/catch counts). Let me count conservatively and split:

- `findLabeledBug(tracker, jiraProject, label)` → array or [] (with try/catch inside, CC ~2)
- `detectTicketKey(runName)` → CC 1
- `hasOpenTicketBug(tracker, jiraProject, ticketKey)` → CC ~2
- `createBugForRun(tracker, jiraProject, run, workflowId, ticketKey, label)` → does create + extract key + labels + link, returns key or null; CC ~6-7 (try/catch around create, newKey check, addLabel try/catch, ticketKey link try/catch, addLabel try/catch). Hmm that's 5+ decisions. Maybe further split `applyBugLinks(tracker, newKey, ticketKey, label)` CC ~3.

Then `processRun(run, ctx)` CC: existing check, ticketKey check, openBug check, key null check → ~4-5. And action: param check, runsRaw null, parse error, empty, loop → ~5.

Alternatively simpler: since raising coverage counts as much as splitting, and the ratchet only requires target CRAP < 30 (from 128.1 / 86.9), I could just write thorough characterization tests achieving high coverage on both functions without any refactor. CRAP with c=11 and cov f: 121(1-f)³+11. For CRAP=30: (1-f)³=19/121=0.157 → f≈46%. So ~50% coverage of detectFailedChecks/action brings them under 30. But the "no function may go UP" gate — no changes needed then. And new functions none.

However the ticket title says "Extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*)" — the ticket's approach is extraction + tests. The AC: "CRAP of both target functions goes down (below the 30 threshold)". Both approaches satisfy. But wait — there's a subtlety with the ratchet: it compares per-function CRAP by name against the released baseline. If I don't refactor, function names stay the same; coverage increases; CRAP goes down. That passes.

But is pure test-only change in the spirit? The ticket explicitly prescribes "Extract pure helpers". Also CRAP thresholds: the quality workflow blocks merge only when functions exceed threshold AND are worse than baseline... Actually the ratchet fails when any function is worse than baseline? Let me recall typical crap4js ratchet semantics: it fails if any function's CRAP exceeds threshold (30) and is not in baseline with same/higher CRAP; improved functions reported. Target: both under 30.

Given "both": extraction reduces CC structurally (more robust against future coverage gaps) and matches the ticket. I'll do extraction + tests, keeping behavior byte-identical in outputs. But every extraction creates NEW functions that must be ≤ 8 CRAP — they're tiny and will be covered by tests.

One concern: exporting helpers for tests. githubHelpers exports many functions; I'll add new exports. workflowFailureReporter exports only action; I'll add helper exports.

So workflowFailureReporter.action has zero coverage → CRAP = CC²+CC = 128.1 means CC=11 (11²+11=132... no). 128.1: solve c²+c=128.1? c=11 → 132; c=10 → 110. Not integer — CRAP formula includes coverage: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov/100)³ + CC. With 0% coverage, 128.1 → c(c+1)=128.1, c≈10.8. Hmm, maybe fractional because... Actually with cov>0: c²(1-f)³+c = 128.1. If c=11: 121·(1-f)³+11=128.1 → (1-f)³=0.968 → f≈1%. OK whatever.

For detectFailedChecks 86.9: c²(1-f)³+c=86.9. c=9: 81(1-f)³+9=86.9 → (1-f)³=0.962 → f≈1.3%. So both have tiny coverage, CC≈11 and CC≈9.

Goal: bring each under CRAP 30. Options: reduce CC by extracting helpers AND/OR raise coverage. "Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it."

Strategy: extract pure helpers with CC ≤ 2 or covered by tests, and write characterization tests covering the branches of the main functions.

CRAP gate: target functions must go DOWN, no function may go UP, new functions must be ≤ 8.

detectFailedChecks keeps: arg parsing dual-mode (branch), headSha null check, scm vs direct fetch (branch), null rawResult return (branch), no checks return, no failures return, per-check loop with jobId match (branch), jenkins branch, try/catch. Reduced CC maybe from 9 → ~6-7. Then cover with tests heavily to push CRAP under 30. CRAP for c=7 at full coverage = 7. With c=7 and 50% coverage: 49·0.125+7 = 13.1. Fine.

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

**Plan for `githubHelpers.detectFailedChecks`:**

Extract pure helpers (all ≤ CC 8, each tiny):

1. `normalizeCheckRunsResult(rawResult)` — parse string, extract array. (CC small)
2. `isFailedCheck(c)` — conclusion failure/timed_out.
3. `appendLogSection(md, fullLogContent, check, logs, label)` → returns {md, fullLogContent} or mutates an accumulator object. Make it pure: takes (check, logs, label) returns {mdSection, fullLogSection} or null.
4. `normalizeLogPayload(raw)` — parse JSON {result} wrapper. (pure)
5. `extractJenkinsTarget(detailsUrl, jenkinsBasePath)` → {jobPath, buildNumber} or null. (pure, CC ~4)
6. `buildCiFailuresMarkdown(failedChecks, headSha, logSections)` — pure builder.
7. `buildResolutionSection()` — constant.

Then detectFailedChecks keeps orchestration: dual-mode arg parse, headSha check, fetch (scm vs direct), null checks, loop calling helpers, try/catch.

But note the ratchet: "new functions must be ≤ 8" and "target functions must go DOWN, no function may go UP". detectFailedChecks CC is ~11; after extraction, remaining branches: try/catch + 2 arg branches + headSha + scm-null + string-parse (moved out) + array extraction (moved out) + no checks + no failures + loop + jobIdMatch + jenkins condition + jenkins inner... Actually if I extract the Jenkins block into `fetchJenkinsLogs(check, jenkinsBasePath)` (CC ~3: guard conditions + loop... the digit-detection loop is a for with 2 branches) and the github-job-logs block into `fetchJobLogs(check, scm, owner, repo)` (CC ~3), the main function drops a lot.

Even better for CRAP: raising coverage counts too. The existing tests cover some Jenkins paths. I'll add characterization tests for: scm-mode invocation, job logs via /jobs/(\d+) match (github + scm), JSON-wrapped logs, no-failures, no checks, null rawResult, string rawResult, unparseable string, headSha missing, overall catch.

**Plan for `workflowFailureReporter.action`:**

Extract helpers:

1. `parseWorkflowRuns(runsRaw)` → {runs: [...]} or {error: '...'} — handles string parse + workflow_runs extraction. (CC ~3)

Actually to be safe under the ratchet for the NEW function (≤8), processRun has: existing.length check, ticketMatch, ticketKey, openBug check, newKey check, ticketKey link/label, try/catch... that's ~8-9. Actually, CRAP ≤ 30 for target functions only required; NEW functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP, not CC. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³+CC. With full coverage CRAP = CC. So new function with CC 8 fully covered = 8 ✓. With CC 9 fully covered = 9 ✗. So keep new functions at CC ≤ 8, and cover them.

processRun: branches: existing>0 (skip), ticketKey null?, openBug>0 (skip), newKey null, addLabel try/catch (catch adds branch? try/catch counts as a branch in most CC tools — crap4js based on escomplex? Unknown. Assume try/catch counts). Let me count conservatively and split:

- `findLabeledBug(tracker, jiraProject, label)` → array or [] (with try/catch inside, CC ~2)
- `detectTicketKey(runName)` → CC 1
- `hasOpenTicketBug(tracker, jiraProject, ticketKey)` → CC ~2
- `createBugForRun(tracker, jiraProject, run, workflowId, ticketKey, label)` → does create + extract key + labels + link, returns key or null; CC ~6-7 (try/catch around create, newKey check, addLabel try/catch, ticketKey link try/catch, addLabel try/catch). Hmm that's 5+ decisions. Maybe further split `applyBugLinks(tracker, newKey, ticketKey, label)` CC ~3.

Then `processRun(run, ctx)` CC: existing check, ticketKey check, openBug check, key null check → ~4-5. And action: param check, runsRaw null, parse error, empty, loop → ~5.

Alternatively simpler: since raising coverage counts as much as splitting, and the ratchet only requires target CRAP < 30 (from 128.1 / 86.9), I could just write thorough characterization tests achieving high coverage on both functions without any refactor. CRAP with c=11 and cov f: 121(1-f)³+11. For CRAP=30: (1-f)³=19/121=0.157 → f≈46%. So ~50% coverage of detectFailedChecks/action brings them under 30. So workflowFailureReporter.action has zero coverage → CRAP = CC²+CC = 128.1 means CC=11 (11²+11=132... no). 128.1: solve c²+c=128.1? c=11 → 132; c=10 → 110. Not integer — CRAP formula includes coverage: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov/100)³ + CC. With 0% coverage, 128.1 → c(c+1)=128.1, c≈10.8. Hmm, maybe fractional because... Actually with cov>0: c²(1-f)³+c = 128.1. If c=11: 121·(1-f)³+11=128.1 → (1-f)³=0.968 → f≈1%. OK whatever.

For detectFailedChecks 86.9: c²(1-f)³+c=86.9. c=9: 81(1-f)³+9=86.9 → (1-f)³=0.962 → f≈1.3%. So both have tiny coverage, CC≈11 and CC≈9.

Goal: bring each under CRAP 30. Options: reduce CC by extracting helpers AND/OR raise coverage. "Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it."

Strategy: extract pure helpers with CC ≤ 2 or covered by tests, and write characterization tests covering the branches of the main functions.

CRAP gate: target functions must go DOWN, no function may go UP, new functions must be ≤ 8.

Plan for detectFailedChecks (CC≈9): extract pure helpers:
- parseCheckRuns(rawResult) — normalize raw to check_runs array (string parse, array, object).

- appendLog pure function — build md + fullLog content given check, logs, label. It mutates md/fullLogContent though. Make it return appended strings or use an accumulator object.

- normalizeLogPayload(raw) — parse JSON {result}.

detectFailedChecks keeps: arg parsing dual-mode (branch), headSha null check, scm vs direct fetch (branch), null rawResult return (branch), no checks return, no failures return, per-check loop with jobId match (branch), jenkins branch, try/catch. Reduced CC maybe from 9 → ~6-7. Then cover with tests heavily to push CRAP under 30. CRAP for c=7 at full coverage = 7. With c=7 and 50% coverage: 49·0.125+7 = 13.1. Fine.
